Innovate

IN-uh-vayt -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, IN. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To innovate to make change with new ideas.

The children's hospital innovates constantly, testing gentler ways to move and monitor its youngest patients.

Worked Example

The third dry summer in a row is killing the seedlings, and drip lines cost more than the whole farm earns. So the farmer punches pinholes in hundreds of used water bottles, buries one beside each plant, and fills them once a week -- and the seedlings live.

The farmer innovated: he made change with a new idea instead of repeating what had always been done. Innovating does not require a laboratory -- it means finding a genuinely new method for an old problem, whether the tool is a satellite or a soda bottle.

How Innovate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

modernize

modernize: to bring something up to date

pioneer

pioneer: to be the first to develop something

experiment

experiment: to try out new approaches

Antonyms

imitate

imitate: to copy what already exists

preserve

preserve: to keep things exactly as they are

How Strong Is It? — experiment → pioneer → innovate

experiment vs. innovate

experiment vs. innovate: Experiment just tries new things and accepts that most will fail, while innovate claims a result: a genuinely new method or idea that actually changes how the work is done.

pioneer vs. innovate

pioneer vs. innovate: Pioneer is the strongest: a company that innovates improves its own products with new ideas, but the one that pioneers a technology is first through the door -- it opens territory nobody had entered at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of innovate.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: in, into (Latin)

root — nov-

root — nov-: new (Latin novus)

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make, to cause to be (Latin -atus)

Put it together

Put it together: Innovate is Latin for 'to bring newness in' -- in- ('into') plus novus ('new'). The word's own anatomy is its definition: an innovator carries something new INTO a field where everyone else is still doing it the old way.

Use the root in a new word: renovate

Use the root in a new word: renovate: The library was renovated over the summer, with new lighting and wider shelves.

Root Check

Word Choice

Innovate is usually intransitive -- companies innovate, teams innovate, chefs innovate -- and it names a HABIT of introducing new ideas, not a single gadget. Keep it distinct from invent: you invent a specific thing, but you innovate when you change the way things are done. Its natural opposites in this unit are stagnation and imitation.
